The biggest and most frustrating issue is SALARY. The hikes are unbelievably low — so low that calling them a hike almost feels like a joke. Even when someone gets a promotion, the salary increase attached to it is so minimal that it barely makes any difference. Many people feel insulted rather than rewarded.
The promotion system is equally disappointing. It does not truly recognize hard work or performance. Promotions often seem to happen by default after certain years instead of based on actual contribution. Someone who works extremely hard the entire year might not get promoted simply because their “cycle” hasn’t arrived yet, while someone else gets promoted just because they have been waiting for years.
The year-end review and rating system is another complete mess. If someone already got promoted recently, they will automatically be given a default “succeeding” rating regardless of how exceptional their work was and that makes their “peanut” hikes become almost invisible. Meanwhile, someone who hasn’t been promoted for years might suddenly receive higher ratings just because it’s their turn. This makes the entire performance evaluation system feel unfair and meaningless.
The most painful part is when you give your full effort, work late hours,solve difficult problems, and genuinely care about your work, only to end up with the same rating as someone who barely worked all year. That completely destroys motivation. 
Because of these issues — pathetic salary hikes, delayed promotions, and a broken rating system — many talented and hardworking employees are leaving the company.The company is slowly losing good people because they simply feel undervalued.
No meaningful hikes, almost no onsite opportunities, and limited career growth.
At the same time, strict policies like hybrid work enforcement are pushed without giving employees proper flexibility for work from home.
Many employees are staying only because of circumstances — not because they believe in the company anymore.
Honestly, it feels like hard work is not rewarded here, and the system is designed to discourage the very people who try the hardest.

benefits.name: Pension
benefits.details: Every employee has a pension plan with us. We have our own pension fund for this, specifically the Stichting Pensioenfonds Capgemini Nederland. The pension plan is non-contributory, which means you do not have to pay anything into it. But if you want to contribute and supplement your pension, you can use the voluntary pension plan.

benefits.name: Mobility
benefits.details: As a consultant, you frequently work for different clients throughout the country. That is why every employee of ours receives a mobility allowance. How you spend this mobility allowance is up to you. You can opt for a leased car, a kilometer allowance for using your own car, or an NS Business Card. Or you could opt to have the amount paid out gross.

benefits.name: Leave
benefits.details: Will you be working full time? Then per calendar year, you will be entitled to 20 statutory days off and 6 days in excess of the legal requirement. We also pay out a vacation allowance once a year. Besides this, you have all the national public holidays off, of course, and Capgemini also provides special paid leave, maternity leave, and parental leave.

benefits.name: Flexible working
benefits.details: Need to drop your children off at school before coming to the office? Or want to start early so that you have time for sports after work? At Capgemini, you are free to decide where and when you work. The laptop, SIM card, and connectivity allowance you receive allow you to log in from anywhere. Of course, it is a good idea to discuss your work times and location with the client for whom you are working.

benefits.name: Salary
benefits.details: We use salary grades at Capgemini. A grade indicates the degree of seniority at Capgemini and serves as the basis for determining your salary. If you join us, you will be assigned to one of our six grades at the start of your career. This depends on your knowledge and experience, of course. A grade is not related to your place in the organization. This means that you genuinely receive recognition for your individual development, knowledge, experience, and level. And not for your position in the hierarchical line.
